data.title: Middle East Eye: Death, displacement and disease: A young Gaza doctor on life under Israeli bombardment
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Death, displacement and disease: A young Gaza doctor on life under Israeli bombardment
A young Palestinian doctor who survived Israel's genocidal war on Gaza has described what it was like confronting the burden of patient care almost immediately after graduating.
In the first episode of Middle East Eye's The Gaza Podcast, which was recorded inside the besieged enclave, Maryam Youssef described the horrors she experienced while volunteering - and living - at Nasser Hospital.
She recalls contracting chickenpox and being forced to isolate in a room for days as bombs rained down around her, and how she has struggled to process the trauma of surviving the conflict.
"I had chickenpox after two days [of starting work at the hospital]," Youssef told podcast host Hussam Tannera.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Two Iranians charged over suspected plot to target Jews in Manchester
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Two Iranians charged over suspected plot to target Jews in Manchester
Two Iranian nationals were charged in Britain with preparing a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in northern England, police said on Friday.
Rahman Salehi, 35, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, have been charged with preparing to commit or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
"It is no secret that this country faces a range of serious threats from the Iranian regime," Home Secretary (interior minister) Shabana Mahmood said in a statement. "They target our Jewish communities and try to silence their critics overseas, often through proxies and criminal networks to hide their involvement."
Iran has always denied such accusations.
Counterterrorism police said Salehi and Ahmadyan had allegedly tried to acquire components and equipment to make an improvised explosive device and conducted reconnaissance on potential targets for attack.
Report by Reuters

data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israeli passengers arrive at Ben Gurion Airport after flydubai suspension
Israeli passengers stranded in Dubai arrived at Ben Gurion Airport on an Arkia Airlines flight, the first since the Emirati airline flydubai suspended the route and Israel's flag carrier El Al cancelled planned repatriation flights, Reuters reported.
The flights were suspended after an Israel-bound flight made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on 30 September, after its co-pilot allegedly attempted to crash the plane.
The flydubai flight was travelling from Dubai to Ben Gurion Airport with 180 passengers on board, most of them Israeli.
About an hour before its scheduled arrival, the plane began a steep descent, dropping from 34,000 feet (10,363 metres) to 16,000 feet (4876.8 metres) in less than two minutes.
It eventually landed safely in Tabuk, in northwestern Saudi Arabia.

data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Settlers kill 19-year-old Palestinian in West Bank, two injured, six detained
Israeli settlers killed 19-year-old Palestinian Bahaa Sami Amin Nathsheh in Kobar, north of the occupied West Bank city of Ramallah, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported, citing the health ministry.
The ministry told Wafa that settlers opened fire at several Palestinians, wounding Nathsheh, who hails from Kafr Aqab town near Jerusalem.
Israeli forces then arrived at the scene and prevented Palestinian medics from providing treatment to the casualty, Wafa said, citing the Palestinian Red Crescent Society.
Another Palestinian was injured after being hit by a tear gas canisters in the head.
Bahaa Sami Amin Nathsheh was fatally shot by settlers in Kobar, north of Ramallah. (Courtesy Wafa)
*Two Palestinians were injured by settlers in Yabrud, east of Ramallah. Wafa reported that the settlers, protected by Israeli forces, attacked the outskirts of the town before the residents attempted to confront the assailants.
*Israeli forces detained six Palestinians from the occupied West Bank governorates of Jerusalem and Tubas, Wafa reported, citing Jerusalem Governorate and the Palestine Prisoner’s Society (PPS).
According to the latest figures from Addameer, the Palestinian Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association, there are currently 9,350 Palestinian political prisoners in Israeli prisons and detention centres, including 350 child prisoners and 90 female prisoners.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump again: 'Iran war could end very soon, probably right after elections'
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Trump again: 'Iran war could end very soon, probably right after elections'
US President Donald Trump has again said that the war with Iran could end soon, "probably right after the elections", while questioning who in Tehran Washington could negotiate with.
Speaking at a rally in Mobile, Alabama, Trump said: "I don't know who the hell to deal with. There's nobody to deal with. Nobody wants to be president. I say, who do I speak to in Iran? … Knock knock, nobody home."
Trump also reiterated that Iran "will never have a nuclear weapon". He added that previous US presidents had failed to act.
"This should have been done by other presidents for years … We always have to do the dirty work," he said.
Trump once again painted a picture of an Iran left defenceless and in deep economic crisis: "They have no navy, they have no air force, they have no radar, they have no anti-aircraft [defence systems]," he said, adding: "Their economy is down the tubes … They have about 310 percent inflation."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Green Party leader Zack Polanski calls for de-proscribing Palestine Action
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Green Party leader Zack Polanski calls for de-proscribing Palestine Action
Green Party leader Zack Polanski has called for Palestine Action to be de-proscribed, SkyNews reported.
"And Greens, we stand with one voice now as we say, drop the charges, end the genocide, de-proscribe Palestine Action," Polanski told a party conference in Brighton to loud applause.
Keir Starmer’s government proscribed Palestine Action in July 2025, meaning that expressing support for or membership of the direct action group - which aimed to cause property damage to companies manufacturing weapons that would be sold to Israel - is a criminal offence that could lead to a prison sentence of up to 14 years.
The Green Party’s annual conference begun in the seaside town of Brighton, just two days after the ruling Labour Party’s conference ended.
Party members are gearing up to vote on an unprecedented motion to declare Zionism a form of racism.
The vote is expected to take place on Sunday, according to party insiders. If the motion passes, it will become official policy and the Greens will become the first major party in the country to recognise Zionism as racism.

An Arkia aircraft brought Israeli passengers stranded in Dubai on Saturday, with an Israir plane expected to follow, while flydubai announced it was suspending all flights to Israel until further notice.
One of the outstanding issues was an Emirati demand that a cargo aircraft accompany the passenger flight to transport passengers’ luggage, Ynet reported.
“They are talking about ‘rescue flights’ as though there is a war in the country. There is no war,” the source told ynet.
He also claimed Emirati officials believe Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking to connect the attack to Iran for political reasons ahead of Israel’s election.
“The feeling in the Emirates is that everything is being done to drag this out because it serves Israel politically,” he said, comparing Israel’s conduct to “an arsonist who runs to start the fire and then runs to put it out.”
Netanyahu had claimed that "a disaster on the scale of September 11" was prevented and the attacker "underwent Islamist radicalisation and came to crash the plane with its passengers on board".
“The one stopping the flights is Israel,” the source said. “If passengers can board an Arkia flight, why not Flydubai?” He argued that Israeli use of the term “rescue flights” created the impression that the UAE was facing a war or emergency. “Rescue from what? From whom? From where?”
According to the source, Etihad is operating eight flights to Abu Dhabi beginning Sunday under a stricter security protocol, and the same procedures could be applied to Flydubai. data.title: Middle East Eye: US sanctions three persons, two charities over alleged Hamas funding
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US sanctions three persons, two charities over alleged Hamas funding
The United States has issued sanctions against three individuals and two France-based charities that it said were part of a network that raised more than $2 million for Hamas, and announced six arrests.
"These designations expose a sophisticated, multi‑year financing architecture that moved more than $2 million to Hamas through deceptive charitable fronts and cryptocurrency channels, demonstrating the organisation's persistent ability to adapt its fundraising mechanisms to evade detection," the US Treasury said in a statement.
Those sanctioned include Saleem Abdallah Saleem al-Zaq, identified as a Hamas member who oversees the financial network and works with the group's media office.
The US Justice Department said French authorities had also arrested sanctioned individuals Faouzi Barika and Amel Oualid, who are linked to the France-based charities Association Baraka and Ensemble C Mieux.
Both charities were also sanctioned in Friday's action. A third person, Nordine Barika, was also arrested by French authorities in the case, the DOJ said.
"Faouzi Barika and Amel Oualid operate from France, where they run purported charities ostensibly to raise money for humanitarian purposes to aid Gazan civilians," the US Treasury said.
In the United States, authorities arrested three men for their alleged funding of Hamas through the network, the DOJ said.
US authorities said the network had raised more than $2 million from 2020 to 2026, of which $1.5 million was raised after the 7 October 2023 attack by Hamas on Israel.
Report by AFP

data.title: Middle East Eye: Gaza hostage deal could have been secured a year earlier, Israeli general says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Gaza hostage deal could have been secured a year earlier, Israeli general says
Israeli Reserve Major General Nitzan Alon, the former government point person on hostage negotiations, has said Israeli hostages in Gaza could have been brought home up to a year earlier, before they were released in late 2025.
“Political and personal considerations” got in the way, Alon said during a conversation hosted by the Washington Institute for Near East Policy on Friday.
Alon has accused the government several times over the past year of delaying or preventing the release of hostages, and has frequently clashed publicly with ministers over responsibility for the deaths of hostages in captivity and the prolonging of the war in Gaza.
He said Israel could have secured the release of all the hostages a year before the final hostage deal, “without it having any impact on the outcome of the war,” while calling for new, “realistic” Israeli leadership.

"Unfortunately the position of the Republican administration is based on wrong assumptions of non-proliferation norms and the IAEA activities."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Gaza aid delay causes chronic shortage of medical supplies, WHO says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Gaza aid delay causes chronic shortage of medical supplies, WHO says
Getting humanitarian aid through Israel into Gaza is layered with "delay after delay", the World Health Organisation said Friday, as it decried "chronic shortages" of medical supplies.
Reinhilde Van de Weerdt, the WHO's representative in the Palestinian territories, said the health situation in the Gaza Strip "remains utterly dire", with none of its hospitals fully functional.
"Not enough humanitarian aid is entering Gaza, and definitely not enough to allow for a meaningful expansion and restoration of health services," she told reporters in Geneva, speaking from Jerusalem.
She said Israel's approval system for medical and other humanitarian supplies was proving a major bottleneck.
"It is laborious, time-consuming, with no guaranteed results," she said.
Based on the WHO's latest analysis, large volumes of medical supplies wait for clearance for a median of 74 days, said Van de Weerdt, adding that if it is not, "than we start that lengthy, cumbersome process all over again".
She added that the approval system kept changing, with new regulations introduced.
Van de Weerdt said standard health kits used worldwide had the lowest approval rate, while X-ray machines, sterilisation equipment and spare parts for CT scans and other essential machinery "get rejected regularly".
"In just the last six months alone, one shipment of prosthetics and assistive devices was rejected four separate times," she said.
However, medicines move "relatively well", with almost 87 percent approved and one percent rejected, she added.
"It's not one single blockage. It's a system, layered with delay after delay... and on the other side of every one of these delays is a patient who is waiting," she said.
"We need the unimpeded and predicable entry of humanitarian and health supplies into Gaza, at scale.
Report by AFP
